declarations.name: parseTsv
declarations.description:
Parses tab-separated text (rows split on newlines) honouring quoted cells,
the inverse of `quoteTsvCell`. A quote only opens a quoted cell at the start
of a field; elsewhere it is literal. Expects line endings already normalised
to "\n" (see `normalizePastedText`).

declarations.name: quoteTsvCell
declarations.description:
Quotes a cell for tab-separated text the way spreadsheets do: cells that
contain a tab, newline or double quote are wrapped in quotes with embedded
quotes doubled, so the cell survives a round trip through `parseTsv`.

declarations.name: safeCssValue
declarations.description:
Guards consumer-supplied values (column widths, option colours) that the grid
interpolates into inline `style` strings. A value is only accepted when it is
a single valid value for the property: anything that could close the
declaration or open another one (`;`, braces, comments, `url(`) is refused.

declarations.name: seedEditorValue
declarations.description:
Write the editor's starting value imperatively.

The editor template must NOT bind `:value` reactively. That makes it a
controlled input, so every FAST render pass writes the model back onto the
element and overwrites whatever the user is typing — cell editing silently
refuses input. The editor owns its value while open; `handleGridInput`
mirrors it back into `editingValue` for commit.

members.name: fillSelection
members.description:
Fills from the current cell selection, or the active cell, without dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
The source extends `count` rows or columns in `direction` and the new cells are filled exactly as
dragging the fill handle there would: the target stops at the first strip with a read-only
cell, the source tiles across it, `cell-fill` is emitted with the same detail, and the filled
range becomes the cell selection. Consumers can call it from a row or cell menu.

members.name: handleColumnHeaderKeydown
members.description:
Handles keydown on a column header: the arrow keys, Home and End move between headers, ArrowDown
returns to the first row in cell focus mode, Shift+Tab returns to the active cell in cell focus mode,
and Ctrl+Alt+R moves focus to the column's resizer. Enter and Space reach the sort button natively.

members.name: handleGridCopy
members.description: Handles the native `copy` event, writing TSV through `clipboardData`.

members.name: handleGridKeydown
members.description:
Returns true to let the browser perform the key's default action.

FAST cancels the default action of any `@event` binding whose expression
does not return exactly `true` (`HTMLBindingDirective.handleEvent`). A
`void` return therefore cancels every keystroke, including characters and
Backspace typed into an open cell editor. Return false only for keys this
handler consumes.

injective and a "-" delimiter between encoded parts is unambiguous.

declarations.name: installFormDisabled
declarations.description:
Teaches a form-associated component to honour `<fieldset disabled>` without
touching the author's own `disabled` attribute or property.

Installs, on the component prototype:
- an observable `fieldsetDisabled` flag (true while an ancestor fieldset disables the control),
- an `effectiveDisabled` getter (`disabled || fieldsetDisabled`) that the component should use
  everywhere it previously read `disabled`,
- `formDisabledCallback`, which the browser invokes when the form-disabled state changes,
- wrappers around `connectedCallback` and `disabledChanged` that re-evaluate the flag, because the
  browser does not call `formDisabledCallback` when the control's own `disabled` already masks the
  fieldset's effect (e.g. inserting or re-enabling inside an already-disabled fieldset).

The component's own `disabledChanged` runs whenever either flag changes. Call once per class,
after the class body and before the element is defined; the class must declare
`fieldsetDisabled` and `effectiveDisabled` for typing.

declarations.name: isDisabledByFieldset
declarations.description:
Returns true when `element` is disabled by an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>`.

Mirrors the HTML "actually disabled" rule: only light-tree ancestors count, and
controls inside a disabled fieldset's first `<legend>` are exempt.

declarations.name: isSafeLinkHref
declarations.description:
Returns true when `href` is safe to render as a link target: an http(s) or
mailto URL, or a relative URL. Everything else (javascript:, data:, vbscript:,
blob:, file:, unparsable values) is rejected.

Uses the URL parser, so obfuscated schemes such as `java\tscript:` are caught.

members.description:
IDREFs in a host `aria-describedby` cannot cross the shadow boundary, so the ids are
resolved in the host's root node and assigned to the input through element reflection
(`ariaDescribedByElements`), together with the supporting text. Without element
reflection only the supporting text is linked, by an IDREF inside the shadow root;
light-DOM targets cannot be referenced in that case.
